subject.title: Prompt-cache prefix churn on OpenAI models: per-turn dynamic injections (message tool hint + volatile system-prompt section) defeat automatic prefix caching

question: Should OpenClaw remove mode-gated `message_tool_only` guidance from OpenAI cache-sensitive system/tool prefixes, or accept the current binding-facts strategy if live telemetry proves it covers the reported production path?
rationale: The fix crosses message-delivery prompting, tool-schema stability, and OpenAI provider cache behavior, and current tests prove only a narrower stabilization path.

options.title: Move guidance out of prefix
options.body: Make tool schemas and the cache-sensitive system prefix stable across delivery modes, with current-turn delivery instructions carried in a late runtime channel or another non-prefix surface.

options.title: Prove current strategy
options.body: Keep the current binding-facts design only if maintainers can show live OpenAI request-prefix hashes remain stable across the reporter's alternating orchestration path.

options.title: Document as limitation
options.body: Leave behavior unchanged but document that `message_tool_only` delivery mode may reduce OpenAI prompt-cache reuse in mixed delivery scenarios.

recommendation.title: Move guidance out of prefix
recommendation.body: Make tool schemas and the cache-sensitive system prefix stable across delivery modes, with current-turn delivery instructions carried in a late runtime channel or another non-prefix surface.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only locally identified recent contributor across the relevant message-tool, system-prompt, and CLI binding surfaces.
